role_and_message.evidence: The three motivation contrasts remain instance separation, point sampling and mask-granularity selection, each exposing a limitation of direct SAM use.

panel_and_object_coverage.evidence: All twelve original scientific regions are retained: four instance-separation images/masks, four sampling examples/masks, and the point prompt plus all three scored ambiguity masks.

labels_math_and_numbers.evidence: Coarse/Refined Coarse mask, Without/With Instance Separation, Confidence based/Our points sampling and SAM scores 96.2, 95.5 and 95.2 retain their source pairings. No score is changed.

connections_and_direction.evidence: The former three side-by-side groups are stacked into three rows. Each without/with or confidence/ours comparison is left-to-right within its row; the ambiguity input precedes the same three candidate masks. No new algorithmic arrow is introduced.

visual_encodings.evidence: Original sampling point cross colors, red/green mask-selection boxes, pink masks and photo overlays are intact protected crops; the green 95.5 selection is not recast as highest SAM score.

examples_and_data.evidence: Independently recomputed all twelve source crop proportional LANCZOS resizes and matched destination pixels, source archive hashes and recorded output hashes. Photographs, sampled locations, silhouette masks and score labels are not generated replacements.

unsupported_additions.evidence: Added statements about splitting instances, improved coverage and highest SAM score not ensuring desired granularity are supported by the original Figure 2 caption. No additional benchmark or quantitative gain is asserted.

complete_visible_content.evidence: All three groups, twelve image/mask regions, three numeric scores and original semantic labels are complete and unobscured in the final PNG.

remaining_limitations: Original scientific regions are proportionally LANCZOS-resampled with documented rounding, not native 1:1 copies. This audit checks fidelity to the supplied figure/text and does not establish the paper claims.
caption:
Figure 2: SAM challenges. Left: As an instance-based model, SAM performs poorly when segmenting a
class comprising multiple instances, see the class “person”. Splitting the class mask into individual instances
addresses this challenge. Middle: Confidence-based sampling (Kweon & Yoon, 2024) yields a suboptimal
mask; in contrast, our proposed sampling strategy achieves comprehensive mask coverage, resulting in im-
proved segmentation. Right: SAM score-based mask selection may not give the best desired segmentation
(see mask in red box). Our mask selection strategy using intersection with the coarse mask determines the
desired mask granularity (see mask in green box).
